analysis.title: ORCL - Ripping the band-aid
key_insights: Barclays reads ORCL's investor day as a significant positive. Guidance of only $10bn of new gross debt through 2030 is much better than the market expected, and added detail on margins and cash flow profiles adds credibility.
Spreads had rallied 25-30bp earlier in the week, which raised the bar for the event. Barclays says ORCL still delivered a stronger and more articulate message than it expected.
Barclays reiterates Overweight on ORCL credit and recommends buying the 2056s. It sees value at current levels, while expecting the market to take a 'fool me twice' approach after the February rally.
In the very near term Barclays expects the structure to trade sideways or give back some of the recent rally as the market braces for a bond deal. It calls the deal potentially a clearing event.
Barclays expects a $10bn all-USD offering. A EUR deal is possible but less likely in this transaction and more likely to be used as a refinancing tool later.

Because the curve is still relatively steep, Barclays prefers the long end. It would not be surprised if the pending deal skews shorter in duration, which could be a catalyst for existing 30y spreads.
ORCL has $20bn of total incremental capital left through 2030, split $10bn debt and $10bn equity. This excludes refinancing of maturities, and total financial debt peaks once the $10bn is raised.

Barclays says investors expected $50-60bn of remaining funding ($20bn in 2027, $30-40bn in 2028, similar to its own model), so the guidance is materially better than expectations. ORCL appears to be the first hyperscaler to say this is the last piece of capital it needs.

CFO Hilary Maxson said ORCL could issue as soon as this year, versus prior guidance of no issuance until 2027. Barclays thinks issuing soon is better, since deal overhang tends to punish hyperscaler spreads.
ORCL plans to add 7GW of capacity between fiscal 2027-28 and end 2028 with 10GW of capacity. Barclays modeled +5.25GW in 2027/28 and 10GW not until 2029.

Higher capacity would normally mean higher capex and funding needs, but the funding guidance implies the opposite. Barclays infers heavier reliance on customer prepays, bring-your-own-hardware (BYOHW) arrangements and vendor financing, none of which the company sized.

Barclays expects vendor financing to draw the most attention and the bears to lean on the 'circular' narrative. It takes a less negative view, citing an undersupplied compute market that gives ORCL leverage to use prepays and BYOHW.

Barclays reads the CFO's comments as meaning no syndicated chip-financing deal from ORCL. It expects direct vendor financing instead, such as leasing chips directly from vendors who keep the receivable.

Barclays floats that OpenAI's Jalapeno chip, deployed at Oracle data centers per Sam Altman, could be a BYOHW lever. If OpenAI uses Broadcom's XPV financing platform for part of its Oracle contract, it would replace ORCL capex with OAI/Broadcom-linked financing and could explain the lack of funding needs.

market_movers.rationale: Barclays reiterates Overweight on ORCL credit and recommends buying the 2056s. Funding needs are far lower than the market feared, and a bond deal soon could clear the overhang.

trade_ideas.description: Buy ORCL 6.7% 02/04/56 bonds (the 2056s), long the long end of the Oracle credit curve
trade_ideas.rationale: Funding needs are much lower than expected, the curve is steep, and the pending bond deal could clear the overhang.
trade_ideas.risk: Larger than expected issuance, less use of alternative funding sources than the market expects, OpenAI struggles or IPO timeline concerns, broader AI worries, and concerns around the equity offering.

risk_factors: Less use of alternative funding sources (prepays, BYOHW) than the market expects.
OpenAI struggles and/or concerns around its IPO timeline.
Vendor financing could draw criticism and feed the 'circular' financing narrative.
Spreads remain wider than before earnings, and the market may take a 'fool me twice' approach after the February rally.
vol_and_positioning: Barclays expects ORCL spreads to pause or give back part of the recent 25-30bp rally in the near term as the market braces for a roughly $10bn USD bond deal, which it says could be a clearing event.
Barclays says the curve is still relatively steep and all-in 30y yields are high, so it prefers the long end and would not be surprised if the new deal skews shorter in tenor.

tension_points.bull_case: Barclays reads the lack of funding needs as a significant positive. An undersupplied compute market lets ORCL lean on customer prepays and BYOHW, and the CFO's comments suggest no syndicated chip-financing deal.
tension_points.bear_case: Bears are expected to lean on vendor financing and the 'circular' narrative. The category is vague, could take forms such as extended payables or direct loans, and ORCL did not size the prepay, BYOHW or vendor financing levers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Larger than expected issuance, or ORCL bringing a syndicated chip-financing deal to market despite the CFO's comments.
